To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the spatial distribution of women’s labour force participation is highly correlated with the spatial distribution of female‐friendly occupations; (ii) this correlation cannot be explained by supply‐side factors; (iii) the correlation between the spatial distribution of occupations and women’s LFPRs is not a spurious correlation, but is a genuine causal relationship; and (iv) female migration does not change the spatial distribution of labour force participation.
